question: where do the GGUF quants readers actually use sit against our EXL3 builds and official FP8, on OUR held-out suite, through ONE shared BF16 head?
why: the standing public critique is that official FP8 is a throughput format whose quality is Q4-to-Q5 class, so beating it is a weak claim; Q8_0 and Q6_K are the honest bar.

suite.shard: shard-0000 of the v5 ladder: contexts 0-511 in the parent's fixed order
suite.note: every candidate below scored the identical 512 contexts and the identical 1,048,064 positions

method.metric: KL(BF16 reference || candidate), full 248,320-entry vocabulary, exact two-pass, float32 within vocabulary chunks and float64 across them
method.head: one shared BF16 lm_head for both operands; no candidate's own head quantization is counted
method.reference: BF16 Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B captured under vLLM at the final norm
method.exl3_candidates: captured under the same vLLM build as the reference, so they carry no cross-engine term
method.gguf_candidates: captured with llama.cpp at pinned commit ece963f41b0b02d7a0d61436ae365762c073a4c8 through tools/gguf_capture.cpp, which reads the post-final-norm state (res->t_embd, src/models/qwen35.cpp) — the same mathematical point the vLLM hook takes; bf16 rounding verified bit-identical to torch on 2,012,449 probe values
method.cross_engine_caveat: a GGUF number therefore contains llama.cpp-versus-vLLM numerics in addition to quantization error, which can only inflate it; the BF16-GGUF engine-floor control that would subtract it is queued, so GGUF rows here are upper bounds and our EXL3 rows are not

findings.q8_is_the_fidelity_leader: Q8_0 measures 0.001087 at 27.05 GiB of serialized weight — 2.5x better than our best build and 4.8x better than official FP8. Anyone who can spare 27 GiB of weights and does not need a long context on a 32 GB card should use it. The critique that Q8 is the honest bar is correct.
findings.fp8_is_a_weak_bar: official FP8 measures 0.005197 while Q6_K measures 0.002035 at 7.2 GiB less serialized weight; on this suite FP8 is beaten by every GGUF point at or above 5 bits. Our published claim of 34-48 % below FP8 stands, and it is a smaller achievement than it sounds.
findings.our_builds_sit_where_a_5_to_6_bit_build_: hydrated 0.002700 at 20.12 GiB of payload lands between Q6_K (0.002035 at 21.31 GiB) and UD-Q5_K_XL (0.004444 at 18.83 GiB), and slightly better than a log-linear interpolation of those two at its own size; the context edition 0.003409 at 19.27 GiB beats UD-Q5_K_XL by 23 % at 0.44 GiB more. So the format advantage at this bitrate is real but modest — nothing like a full bit on this suite.
findings.tail_ordering_matches_mean_ordering: p99.9 runs 0.0351 (Q8_0) < 0.0794 (Q6_K) < 0.1313 (hydrated) < 0.1447 (online) < 0.1632 (context) < 0.2144 (Q5_K_XL) < 0.2440 (FP8) < 0.5576 (K4), i.e. the same order as the means with one crossing: our three builds are lighter-tailed than UD-Q5_K_XL and FP8 despite the context build being close to Q5_K_XL on the mean.
findings.what_this_does_not_settle: the GGUF rows are upper bounds until the BF16-GGUF engine-floor control is measured; the comparison is text-only teacher-forced fidelity and says nothing about serving a 262,144-token multimodal context on a 32 GB card, which is where these artifacts actually differ.
